physicalNotes: Radius 0.21679045 Jupiter radii from Barkaoui et al. 2023 (2023A&A...677A..38B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..38B/abstract): 15,498.8 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0204 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Barkaoui et al. 2023 (2023A&A...677A..38B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARKAOUI_ET_AL_2023): P 4.9019804 d
sources.shape: Barkaoui et al. 2023 (2023A&A...677A..38B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARKAOUI_ET_AL_2023): a/R* 30.79; Barkaoui et al. 2023 (2023A&A...677A..38B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARKAOUI_ET_AL_2023): inclination 89.43 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Barkaoui et al. 2023 (2023A&A...677A..38B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARKAOUI_ET_AL_2023): transit mid-time 2459483.65667 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 2 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
